correctness.rationale: Let g(x)=h((1+x)/2), H(s)=g(sqrt(s)). The analytic derivative H(s)=−(sqrt(s)/(1−s)−artanh(sqrt(s)))/(4s^{3/2})<0 proves strict concavity on 0<s<1. For orthonormal axes squares s1+s2+s3=1, Jensen gives maximum H(1/3)=beta*, and concavity at simplex vertices gives minimum 2ln2/3. For arbitrary axes, test r=n_i to bound Bmin, equality forces all axes orthogonal. For Bmax singular 3x3 axis matrix A admits r in ker A giving ln2>beta*. For invertible A, trace(C)=3, C=AA^T; averaging over sign epsilon gives average ||A^{-1}epsilon/sqrt3||²=tr(C^{-1})/3≥1, strict unless C=I. A norm>1 witness yields a normalized r with all |n_j·r|<1/sqrt3, so Bmax>beta*. Independent symbolic Hessian sign checks and a nonorthogonal exact frame test corroborate strictness; proof is analytic for every triple.
residual_risks: Only pure states, equally weighted three projective binary bases; not general POVMs or higher dimensions.

value.rationale: The precise first nontrivial dimension and three complementary measurements are central to entropic certainty theory. Both global extremal directions and exact uniqueness settle a named conjectural special case, not merely re-evaluate the known MUB points.

final_claim: Among all triples of rank-one projective qubit measurement bases, pairwise mutually unbiased axes uniquely maximize B_min (state-minimum averaged Shannon entropy) at (2/3)ln2 and uniquely minimize B_max (state-maximum) at beta*=h((1+1/sqrt3)/2). Thus both extrema of Conjecture 1 at N=2, L=3 hold with rigidity.
limitations: Qubit pure states and three equally weighted rank-one projective measurements only.
